title: Desk Guidance — Estimated Water Reads on the Utility Pass-Through Service
content:
**Guidance.** When a water submeter on a Utility Pass-Through Service account could not be read on its read day, the desk records an estimated water read for that read cycle so that the cycle can be billed. The desk works out the estimated water consumption for the cycle from the published utility policies and the account's records, and records it as one estimated water read for the statement month on which the cycle is billed.

## What the recorded read does

- It enters one estimated water read for the statement month given, standing in for the read day that was missed.
- The read starts from the prior register reading supplied and carries the estimated consumption supplied; its register reading becomes the prior reading plus that consumption.
- Recording the read does not bill it and does not change the utility balance. The read appears in the account's ledger as an estimated water read that a usage charge can bill.

## Invoking the tool

The tool is `post_estimated_water_read_4835faa0`, an agent-side tool. The desk unlocks it and then calls it itself.

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `utility_account_id` | Reference number of the resident's utility account, as returned by the utility account lookup for this resident | Id |
| `billing_period` | Statement month on which the estimated read is billed | YYYY-MM |
| `read_date` | Date of the read day the estimate stands in for | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `prior_reading` | Register reading the estimated consumption is measured from — the latest register reading on the account's water reads | Decimal register reading in thousand gallons, 2 decimal places, as shown in the ledger |
| `consumption` | Estimated water consumption for the cycle | Decimal in thousand gallons (kgal), 2 decimal places, already rounded half up to the hundredth |

## What comes back

A receipt containing `utility_entry_id` (reference number of the new estimated read, which a usage charge uses as the read it bills), `billing_period` (YYYY-MM), `entry_date` (the read day, YYYY-MM-DD), `read_type` (always "estimated"), `prior_reading` and `current_reading` (register readings, thousand gallons, 2 decimal places) and `consumption` (kgal, 2 decimal places). A returned `utility_entry_id` means the read is recorded.

## Desk Q&A

**Does recording the estimate put a charge on the statement?** No. The read is recorded without billing it, and the utility balance does not move.

**Which register reading is the starting point?** The latest register reading on the account's water reads; the new read's register reading is that figure plus the estimated consumption.

**Which date goes in as the read date?** The read day that the estimate stands in for.
